newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CNI says trade, fiscal outlook worsening.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CNI says trade, fiscal outlook worsening.

text.p: Brazil's National Industry Confederation (CNI) said Monday imbalances in the fiscal situation and trade performance were set to get worse in 1997.
The CNI said however that shortfalls in the external accounts were manageable and it cautioned against monetary tightening to suppress demand.

"The most recent data on trade and the public accounts has been negative, suggesting a worsening and not a correction in the imbalances that characterize the current state of the Brazilian economy," it said in its monthly report.
"In order not to damage the mid and long-term adjustments, measures to restrict consumption must be fundamentally fiscal and not monetary," it said.
The CNI said end-December figures showed the economy was expanding but not at a rate that suggested overheating.

As far as the fiscal situation was concerned, the CNI said a decline in the public sector's primary surplus up to end-November last year showed an "undeniable deterioration" in the government's accounts.

The industry group said the current debate about braking the economy to close the trade deficit should keep in mind that economic expansion in the first quarter of 1997 did not seem as "intense" as it did in early 1995.

It added that the economy could probably not cope with a sharp monetary shock which would not only depress domestic consumption but also hit foreign investors, thus impacting on Brazil's ability to finance its current account gap.
"The public sector...would also be strongly hit by an increase in interest rates, widening the deficit and increasing public debt," the report added.
Through November, the public sector posted a consolidated operational deficit of 3.91 percent of gross domestic product versus a 4.27 percent deficit in the same year-ago period.

In primary terms the government ended November in equilibrium against a surplus of 0.94 percent of GDP up to end-November 1995. The CNI put last year's primary surplus at 0.4 percent ((--Michael Christie, Brasilia newsroom 55-61-2230358))
